macro.story:
The tape is in a tricky transitional zone. SPY at 733 is still above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages and the broader regime remains a bull (drawdown only 1.7% off highs), but underneath the surface momentum is fading: SPY's MACD has flipped below its signal line with a negative histogram, RSI sits at 46.7, and Bollinger bands place price below the midline. The Nasdaq has lost its 50-day, and QQQ is down 2.5% over five sessions. Yet the Dow and Russell 2000 are bucking the trend with bullish MACD and RSIs in the 60s — a classic rotation tell, not an outright breakdown.

The dominant cross-asset driver grounded in the active themes is the AI Infrastructure capex cycle in its CHASING stage, layered with the geopolitical risk unwind from the Iran/Hormuz resolution. WTI crude has collapsed 25.6% over 21 days into the $69 zone with RSI at 25.6, validating the supply-shock-unwind thesis. That should be unambiguously risk-on — yet the dollar is the spoiler: DXY at 101.7 with RSI 77.4 (overbought) has ripped 2.5% in 21 days and is dragging gold and silver into deep washouts (Gold -11.2%/21d, Silver -25%/21d, both with RSI in the high 20s). The validated DXY-up-equals-metals-down inverse relationship is on full display.

Volatility tells the real story. VIX at 18.05 is contained but its 21-day change is +6%, and the VIX3M/VIX term structure is in contango — futures pricing more risk further out. The 10Y/2Y spread has compressed 42% over 21 days, with the 2Y stickier than the 10Y as front-end yields hold up. This is not a euphoric tape, but it isn't a washout either — Engine C reads CALM with SPY 6.9% above its 200-day and breadth at 77.8%. The validated washout-bounce combo is NOT in place (RSI not below 30, no breadth thrust). Confidence is LOW because trend says one thing (still up) while momentum, the dollar, and term structure say another.

The playbook: lean on the validated Early-Runway rotation signals in Financials, Industrials, and select consumer-cyclical pockets where the cross-sectional bid is real. Avoid chasing extended commodity-sensitive longs while DXY is overbought. Treat new entries as smaller, geometry-driven, and stop-respecting.
